28 EPISODES DONE AND DUSTED...PLENTY MORE TO COME. 

The first 28 episodes of The Business of Being an Author podcast are now well and truly out in the world, and I have to say, I absolutely love doing this show.

When we started, I wanted to create a podcast that went much deeper than simply talking about how to write and publish a book. There’s plenty of information out there about that.

I wanted to talk about what happens when we start thinking of our book as something much bigger.

How do we write smart, commercially focused books that become powerful business assets? How do we use those books to build credibility and authority, attract the right clients, create speaking opportunities, open doors, start conversations and ultimately build a bigger business around our ideas?

And, of course, how do we become really good at leveraging our books once we’ve created them?

That’s the business of being an author.

So far, the podcast has had two main types of episodes.

There are the deep-dive teaching episodes, where I unpack a particular aspect of writing, publishing, positioning and leveraging a commercially focused book.

Then there are the strategic interviews with authors, where we get behind the book itself and talk about the decisions they’ve made, what has worked, what hasn’t, and how their books are creating opportunities for them.

And coming very soon, we’re adding a third type of episode, conversations with industry experts who can help authors better understand the rapidly changing world of publishing, marketing, media, business and beyond.

A huge thank you to all of the wonderful guests who have joined me for these first 28 episodes (list below) and to Chris Ashmore, our brilliant show producer, and Lalita Lowe, our equally brilliant show manager, who both do so much behind the scenes to make the podcast happen. 

And thank you to everyone who has listened, shared an episode or sent me a message about something you’ve taken away from the show. It means a lot.

If you’re an author, aspiring author, or someone who believes a book could become an important part of your business and your future, there are now 28 episodes waiting for you.

The Business of Being an Author is available on all the major podcast platforms. And here's a direct link - https://lnkd.in/gRSwEPmu

And we’re only getting started.

Cheers,
Andrew

The fear of sounding stupid can keep us from saying what we really think.

When we’re worried about how other people are judging us, there can be a tendency to put them in first place and ourselves in second.

I describe it as “deifying the other and crucifying yourself.”

And at some point, we need to see that this is BS.

Instead, we can begin developing an inner authority.

“I serve others. I trust myself. I don’t expect others to trust me.”

Reversing an old pattern like this doesn’t happen all at once. It starts with concrete action. Saying the thing. Asking the question. Taking the chance that you might not sound perfect.

And slowly, we stop letting other people run our inner show.

How often has the fear of sounding stupid kept you from speaking up?

If this feels familiar, explore it further with the Awareness That Heals AI Companion. It can help you slow down, reflect and find your own wisdom.
